title: Loneliness is becoming a policy category, but national recognition has not yet become evaluated social infrastructure
source_unit: Goldman et al., National policy responses to address loneliness: A global scoping review of 194 WHO member states, Health Policy 165 (2026), 105553
geography: Global review of national policies across 194 WHO Member States; included policy documents from selected high-income countries

observations.period: Policy landscape through February 2025; global coverage of loneliness policy

denominator.unit: WHO Member States searched for national policies directly addressing loneliness, social isolation, or social connection

direct_policy_states.unit: WHO Member States with policies directly addressing loneliness, social isolation, or social connection

direct_policy_share.unit: percent of 194 WHO Member States with a directly addressing national policy in the review

included_documents.unit: documents from eight Member States included in the in-depth policy analysis

mechanism.value: Loneliness is being recognized as a societal and public-health challenge, but dedicated national policy remains concentrated and sparse

observations.method: Scoping review of government websites in all 194 WHO Member States using defined search terms, followed by matrix extraction, document analysis, and policymaker validation.
observations.uncertainty: Policy-document visibility, language, terminology, expired links, and the exclusion of loneliness content embedded in broader health or social policies may understate national activity; policy presence is not implementation.
observations.subgroup: National governments and policy systems across WHO Member States, with the included dedicated policies concentrated in high-income countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Countries may address loneliness through mental-health, ageing, public-health, social, housing, transport, or community policies without labeling it as a standalone issue; dedicated-policy absence does not mean no action.

observations.period: Included national policies; common aims and intervention routes

denominator.unit: Member States with directly addressing policy documents included in the analysis

awareness_and_stigma.value: All included countries identified raising awareness and reducing stigma as a common aim

individual_and_organization_support.value: All included countries supported both individuals and organisations to manage loneliness

community_local_approaches.value: Stronger communities and local approaches appeared in policies from Denmark, Finland, Japan, Scotland, Wales, the Netherlands, and the USA

cross_sectoral_collaboration.value: Cross-sector collaboration among government, private, and third-sector actors appeared in policies from Denmark, England, Germany, Japan, Sweden, and the USA

mechanism.value: The policy response is moving from individual coping toward community infrastructure, organizational capacity, and cross-sector coordination

observations.method: Comparative qualitative analysis of the included national strategies, action plans, priority plans, and advisories.
observations.uncertainty: Policy aims and recommendations do not establish funded delivery, reach, local capacity, or effectiveness; country comparisons reflect different documents and institutional contexts.
observations.subgroup: National and local governments, civil-society organizations, private-sector partners, health and social-care systems, and people experiencing loneliness or social isolation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Community-based approaches can shift responsibility to under-resourced local organizations, while individual supports may remain essential for people facing severe or persistent isolation.

observations.period: 2018-2025; timing and political origins of national loneliness policies

denominator.unit: Member States with directly addressing policy documents in the review

recent_policy_emergence.value: Most included policies were published in 2023, with earlier examples beginning in 2018

policy_origins.value: Policies emerged following societal activism, government-department initiatives, or a large-scale research project

research_and_data.value: Several policies called for research or improved knowledge to strengthen action and measurement

mechanism.value: Loneliness becomes governable when social concern, institutional sponsorship, and evidence infrastructure align

observations.method: Document chronology and qualitative comparison of national policy origins and stated priorities.
observations.uncertainty: The review describes policy emergence but does not identify a causal sequence between activism, research, government sponsorship, and adoption; chronology is not impact evidence.
observations.subgroup: National policy actors, researchers, civil-society advocates, local organizations, and populations targeted by national strategies.
observations.counterinterpretation: A policy may be adopted symbolically or in response to political attention without a durable budget, implementation mandate, or local delivery network.

observations.period: 2026 review conclusion; evaluation and implementation boundary

denominator.unit: Member States with directly addressing policies included in the in-depth analysis

rigorous_effectiveness_evaluation.unit: included national policies with rigorous evaluation of effectiveness identified by the review

funding_requirement.value: The review concludes that adequate funding is required to maximise policy impact

evidence_gap.value: The policy field has more stated interventions than rigorous evidence about which national strategies work, for whom, and through which local routes

mechanism.value: Recognition can outrun implementation and evaluation, creating a legitimacy risk if governments name connection as a priority without resourcing delivery or demonstrating results

observations.method: Scoping-review assessment of the policy documents and their stated or available evaluation evidence.
observations.uncertainty: No evaluation identified does not prove no local or unpublished evaluation exists; the review does not estimate policy effectiveness or compare outcomes across countries.
observations.subgroup: People experiencing loneliness or social isolation, organizations delivering community interventions, health and social-care systems, and national/local funders.
observations.counterinterpretation: Policy adoption may still coordinate services, reduce stigma, or create future evaluation capacity before measurable population outcomes are available.

related_sources.claim: WHO Commission report establishing the global public-health framing for social connection.
PubMed record for the peer-reviewed 2026 scoping review.

boundary: This record adds a global policy-capacity route from loneliness recognition through national strategies, community infrastructure, cross-sector collaboration, funding, and evaluation. It is a scoping review of publicly available policy documents, not a prevalence estimate, intervention evaluation, causal health study, or proof that dedicated national policy improves social connection.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The open-access article PDF was reviewed for the 194-state search universe, document inclusion, eight-state policy subsample, common policy aims, origins, and evaluation/funding conclusions.
